title: Right triangles inside bigger figures
summary: Spot which triangles in a composite figure are right-angled — then use Pythagoras one triangle at a time.
alt: A figure with a right angle at C, a point P on BC, and the triangles APC, ABC and ABP.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: A figure made of triangles
steps.narration: Here is a figure with a right angle at **C**, and a point **P** on the line **BC**. Joining **A** to **P** makes several triangles inside one figure: **ΔAPC**, **ΔABC** and **ΔABP**. Which of them can we use Pythagoras' Theorem on?

steps.title: ΔAPC — right-angled
steps.narration: **ΔAPC** has the right angle at **C**, so it **is** right-angled. Its hypotenuse is **AP** (opposite C), so Pythagoras' Theorem works here: \[ AP^2 = PC^2 + AC^2 \]

steps.title: ΔABC — right-angled
steps.narration: **ΔABC** has the same right angle at **C** — it is the bigger triangle, and **BC = BP + PC**. Its hypotenuse is **AB**: \[ AB^2 = BC^2 + AC^2 \]

steps.title: ΔABP — NOT right-angled
steps.narration: **ΔABP** has **no** right angle (the angle at P is not 90°, and nothing else is marked). So we **cannot** use Pythagoras' Theorem directly in ΔABP.

steps.title: One right triangle at a time
steps.narration: Strategy: split the figure into right-angled triangles and work through them **one at a time**. Start with the triangle whose two sides you know — its answer then feeds the next triangle.

formulas.title: In ΔAPC  (∠C = 90°)
formulas.text: AP is the hypotenuse of ΔAPC.

formulas.title: In ΔABC  (∠C = 90°)
formulas.text: AB is the hypotenuse of ΔABC.

challenges.title: Which triangle is not right-angled?
challenges.prompt: In the figure, ∠C = 90° and P lies on BC. Which triangle is **not** right-angled?
challenges.hint: Look for a triangle that has the marked right angle as one of its corners.
challenges.explain: ΔAPC and ΔABC both have the right angle at C. ΔABP does not, so Pythagoras' Theorem cannot be used directly in it.

challenges.title: Hypotenuse of ΔAPC
challenges.prompt: Which side is the hypotenuse of **ΔAPC**?
challenges.hint: It is opposite the right angle at C.
challenges.explain: The side opposite ∠C in ΔAPC is **AP**.

challenges.title: The whole base
challenges.prompt: P lies on BC between B and C. How do the lengths on the base fit together?
challenges.hint: BC is made of two pieces laid end to end.
challenges.explain: BC = BP + PC — add the pieces before using Pythagoras in ΔABC.

intro: Many problems give a figure made of several triangles. First find the **right angles**; only a right-angled triangle can use Pythagoras' Theorem.
takeaways: Mark **every right angle** in the figure first.
Only triangles that contain a right angle can use Pythagoras' Theorem — ΔABP above cannot.
Work through the right-angled triangles **one at a time**; each answer feeds the next.
Lengths on a straight line add up: **BC = BP + PC**.

notes.title: Exam tip
notes.text: Write "In ΔAPC, ∠C = 90°. Using Pythagoras' Theorem," before each calculation so it is clear which triangle you are using.
